landing.description: Optimizing safety and visitor experience in Cartagena through advanced graph algorithms and combinatorial logic.
landing.ttdp_description: The Tourist Trip Design Problem (TTDP) is an optimization challenge that seeks the perfect route considering interests, time, and budget. In Muralla App, we face the challenges of the Historic Center (narrow streets, high density, and emergency risks) to ensure efficient evacuations and safe tours.

about.title: About the Project
about.importance_p1: The Historic Center of Cartagena de Indias is an architectural jewel that attracts thousands of tourists. However, it faces challenges in emergency management due to its high population density and the complexity of its narrow streets.
about.importance_p2: Our application determines the best evacuation routes using the P-graph (Process Graph) model, originally designed for industrial networks and adapted here for the Combinatorial Optimization of human flows.
about.subtitle: Project Importance
about.description_1: The Historic Center of Cartagena de Indias is an architectural jewel that attracts thousands of tourists. However, it faces challenges in emergency management due to its high population density and the complexity of its narrow streets.
about.description_2: Our application determines the best evacuation routes using the P-graph (Process Graph) model, originally designed for industrial networks and adapted here for the Combinatorial Optimization of human flows. This is essential for Life Protection, Resource Optimization by authorities, and Congestion Reduction on main roads.

instructions.title: User Guide
instructions.step1_desc: The grid is fundamental for space discretization. Activate the switch in the "Editor" tab to deploy the reference mesh. Each cell represents an area of influence for density calculation.
instructions.step2_desc: Define network nodes. Click to add points of interest (POIs) or decision points. Connect them to form edges, defining flow capacity and travel time between them.
instructions.step3_desc: Select between Dijkstra (shortest path) or Ford-Fulkerson (maximum flow). Click on Origin and Destination. The system will calculate the optimal route highlighting it in neon colors for maximum visibility.
instructions.step4_desc: Use Resolve Graph to send the graph to the P-graph engine. You will get a catalog of alternative solutions. Perfect for evaluating parallel routes in case of obstructions on the main road.
instructions.step5_desc: Switch to the Heat Map layer to visualize critical congestion zones. This analysis is vital to predict where people will accumulate and redirect them before a blockage occurs.
instructions.faq_q1: Why are my routes not saved?
instructions.faq_a1: This version 2.0 saves data in local memory (SessionStorage). If you refresh the page without exporting the GeoJSON file, network changes will be lost.
instructions.faq_q2: How do I edit an existing edge?
instructions.faq_a2: Simply click on the line connecting the nodes. An interactive panel will allow you to adjust the weight (distance) and capacity (road width).
instructions.faq_q3: What does the neon color mean?
instructions.faq_a3: Neon green indicates the Origin node and fuchsia indicates the Destination node. Your optimal route will appear highlighted to differentiate it from the base road network.
instructions.faq_q4: How do I load the real map?
instructions.faq_a4: Use the "Load Cartagena (Full)" button in the editor sidebar. This will load a predefined graph with the most important points of interest in the center.
